meta.title: Welsh local elections 2027: research data for Local Record
meta.method: Web search and fetch only. Figures are copied from the cited sources. Nothing is estimated. Where sources conflict, both are noted.

partyKeys.other: Independents, local groups and minor parties combined (Open Council Data's 'Independent / Other')

sources.says: Local Government | 6 May 2027 | Photo ID not needed
Thursday 6 May 2027; 22 Welsh councils, whole-council elections

termLength.says: Local elections are now held every 5 years, whereas previously they were held every 4 years.

franchise.summary: Voting age 16. British, Irish, EU and qualifying Commonwealth citizens, and citizens of other countries who are legally resident (have permission to live in the UK or do not need it).
franchise.note: Votes at 16 and for qualifying foreign citizens came in under the Local Government and Elections (Wales) Act 2021 and already applied at the May 2022 council elections. Not new for 2027.

automaticVoterRegistration.summary: Welsh Government laid regulations (24 June 2026) to roll out automatic voter registration for the local government register across all Welsh councils for the 2027 elections, after pilots in Carmarthenshire, Gwynedd, Newport and Powys. Councils will identify eligible people by data matching, notify them and their right to opt out, then add them.
automaticVoterRegistration.commencement: Regulations 'expected to come into force this Autumn' (2026). Whether they are now in force was not confirmed.

votingSystem.system: First past the post (single-member wards); plurality block voting in multi-member wards
votingSystem.summary: The 2021 Act lets each council choose STV by a two-thirds vote of all its members. Three councils consulted and voted; all three votes failed. No council will use STV in 2027.

councilVotes.note: Consultation (12 Aug to 30 Sep 2024) found 60.5% for STV. Decision needed before 15 Nov 2024 for 2027.
The council's news page is dated 15/11/2024. The fetch tool read the meeting date as 14 November 2023, which looks like a misreading; check the page.

boundaryChanges.summary: Most councils keep the wards used in 2022 (set by the 2021-22 electoral arrangements orders). The Welsh Government accepted Democracy and Boundary Commission Cymru final recommendations for three councils without changes, to take effect for May 2027: Vale of Glamorgan, Carmarthenshire and Caerphilly.

ministerialDecision.by: Siân Gwenllian MS, Cabinet Minister for Local Government, Housing and Planning
ministerialDecision.says: implemented without modification ... taking effect in readiness for the May 2027 Local Government elections

boundaryChanges.ordersMade: Not confirmed. As at 24 June 2026 the orders were being drafted. No made electoral arrangements order for these three councils was found on legislation.gov.uk. The 2026 orders found (WSI 2026 No. 87, 95, 102) are community orders, not council ward orders.

councils.note: The Commission and the council's cabinet report give the existing figure as 58 councillors across 26 wards, but 54 councillors were elected in 2022 and 54 seats appear in every composition source. The 58 is unexplained; check it.
Final councillor and ward numbers not verified (they are in the final report PDF, which could not be read). The draft proposed 74 councillors in 47 wards, down from 75 in 51.

The Commission's news item gives 24 multi-member wards (12 two-member, 10 three-member, 2 four-member), which totals 62, not 68. Single-member wards are presumably not counted in that list; total ward count not verified.

totalSeats2027.note: Not confirmed. If the Vale goes 54 to 59 and Caerphilly 69 to 68, and Carmarthenshire's final figure is unknown, the total cannot be stated. Pollcheck gives 1,238 seats; Wikipedia gives 1,234 (the current total). Neither shows its working.

current.controlCounts: Labour majority: 7 (Blaenau Gwent, Caerphilly, Cardiff, Newport, Rhondda Cynon Taf, Swansea, Torfaen). Plaid Cymru majority: 3 to 4 (Ceredigion, Gwynedd, Isle of Anglesey; Carmarthenshire disputed). No overall control or minority: the rest. See each council's notes.

election2022.source: Sum of the 22 per-council Wikipedia articles
election2022.note: The per-council sum gives Labour 528 against 526 in the Wales-wide table, which also lists 2 seats as vacant after the election. Independents plus others match (316). The most likely explanation is that 2 postponed contests later went to Labour and are counted in the council articles; this is not verified. The Electoral Reform Society gives slightly different national totals (Ind 310, PC 200, Other 8, total 1,232): https://electoral-reform.org.uk/?p=6902

polling.seneddPollsNote: Only three Senedd polls have been published since the 7 May 2026 election. The 2026 Senedd election used a closed-list system with one vote per voter, so there is no constituency/list split. All polls are online panels of adults aged 16+ in Wales.

polling.westminsterPollsNote: Only one Wales Westminster poll with full figures was verified. Pollcheck's 3-poll average (as at 30 Sep 2026) is Reform 25.7, Plaid 22.0, Labour 19.7, Con 15.0, Green 8.7, which implies two other recent Westminster polls (Survation and More in Common are named), but their figures could not be read. More in Common reports Reform would be the largest party in Wales at a general election, without figures.

senedd2026.system: Closed party lists, 16 six-member constituencies, 96 Members (D'Hondt)
senedd2026.government: Plaid Cymru minority; Rhun ap Iorwerth elected First Minister on 12 May 2026
senedd2026.note: Votes and shares match the sum of ITV's 16 constituency tables. Seats for Plaid, Reform, Labour and Green confirmed by ITV; Conservative 7 and Lib Dem 1 from Wikipedia only (they make the total 96). Turnout 51.6% confirmed by Senedd Research. The six-member, D'Hondt detail comes from the Senedd Cymru (Members and Elections) Act 2024 and was not re-checked in this session.

byElections.source: Open Council Data UK by-election archive
caveats: Open Council Data says its list 'may not be comprehensive and doesn't always include by-elections on May election days'.
Dates are Open Council Data's record dates. They are often a day or more after polling day (e.g. Saron: polling 22 Oct 2026, recorded 23 Oct).

'fromParty' is the outgoing councillor's affiliation at the time of the vacancy, after any defections, so it is not always the party that won in 2022. Wikipedia sometimes reports the same contest against the 2022 party (e.g. Powys Yscir: Wikipedia 'LD gain from Con', OCD 'Reform to LD').
Gwynedd Bethel a'r Felinheli (Nov 2025): Open Council Data records Plaid to 'People's Administration'; Wikipedia records a Plaid hold. Unresolved.
Party labels are shortened: FPV = Flintshire People's Voice.

conflictsAndGaps: Denbighshire: new leader Hugh Evans (Sept 2026); administration make-up unverified; WLGA lists him as Labour, other sources Independent.
Carmarthenshire: Plaid majority (OCD, 39/75) vs no overall control with a Plaid/Independent coalition (Wikipedia). Labour's current seat count differs (OCD 14, Wikipedia Aug 2025 18).
Merthyr Tydfil: OCD 'IND min' vs Labour minority led by Brent Carter (WLGA, council, Wikipedia).
Bridgend: Wikipedia 'Labour majority' vs OCD Labour 25/51 (minority).
Swansea: OCD not updated for the June 2026 Mumbles result.
Vale of Glamorgan: Commission and council report show 58 existing councillors; 2022 election and all composition sources show 54.
Carmarthenshire final ward review numbers not verified; Caerphilly ward breakdown in the Commission news item does not add up.
Electoral arrangements orders for the three reviewed councils not found as made.
Total seats in 2027 not confirmed (1,234 now; Pollcheck says 1,238).
Post-election Senedd polls: sample sizes for More in Common and YouGov (Sept 2026) not found; fieldwork dates for YouGov Sept 2026 not found.
